If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.7) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 2–5% in early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is neutral (±0.3) and forecast is trending upward, reduce late horizon (15–30 days) by 3–7% to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase late horizon (15–30 days) by 3–7% to offset underestimation.  
If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, reduce mid-horizon (8–14 days) by 5–10% to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is consistently positive but price is declining, increase mid-horizon (8–14 days) by 3–6% to compensate for sentiment-driven overconfidence.
